skill.name: flutter-build-responsive-layout
skill.description: Build adaptive Flutter interfaces with LayoutBuilder, MediaQuery, flexible widgets, responsive breakpoints, and width constraints for mobile, tablet, and desktop windows.
skill.summary: Create Flutter layouts that respond to available space across mobile and large-screen form factors.
skill.author: flutter

content.value_statement: Rigid Flutter interfaces overflow or stretch across changing window sizes. This skill guides adaptive layouts using constraints, breakpoints, flexible widgets, and large-screen width limits.
actual_capabilities: Selects LayoutBuilder or MediaQuery based on the space being measured.
Guides breakpoint-based widget trees for compact and large widths.
Uses Expanded, Flexible, and BoxConstraints to control widget sizing.
Adapts lists into responsive grids with lazy rendering.
Constrains and centers content for readable large-screen layouts.
Reviews orientation, keyboard, mouse, trackpad, and touch behavior.
limitations: Does not inspect or run a Flutter project automatically.
Does not define universal breakpoints for every product or design system.
Does not replace testing on real devices, resizable windows, and accessibility settings.
Provides layout guidance, not complete navigation or state-management architecture.

use_cases.title: Adapt a Mobile Screen
use_cases.description: Convert a fixed mobile widget tree into compact and wide layouts based on available width.

use_cases.title: Improve Tablet and Desktop Layouts
use_cases.description: Replace stretched lists and forms with responsive grids, centered content, and practical width limits.

use_cases.title: Review Responsive Behavior
use_cases.description: Assess breakpoints, overflow risks, orientation behavior, input methods, and large-screen readability before release.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Responsive Widget
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain whether this Flutter screen should use LayoutBuilder, MediaQuery, Expanded, or Flexible. Describe the available-space requirement and current widget tree.
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose the correct foundation for a simple responsive change.

prompt_templates.title: Create Compact and Wide Layouts
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Flutter widget into compact and wide layouts. Use a justified breakpoint and preserve existing behavior and accessibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: Adapt a fixed mobile screen for tablets and desktop windows.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Large-Screen Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this list or form for large screens. Add sensible width constraints, centering, and responsive grid behavior where appropriate.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prevent excessive stretching while keeping content efficient and readable.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Responsive Flutter Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these related Flutter screens across narrow, medium, and wide widths. Identify overflow, breakpoint, navigation, input, orientation, and performance issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform an advanced review across a multi-screen application flow.

output_examples.input: A product list uses one column at every width and looks sparse on desktop.
output_examples.output: A responsive plan with a lazy grid, width-based column sizing, preserved item behavior, and checks for narrow-window overflow.

output_examples.input: A registration form stretches across a tablet and desktop window.
output: Center the form within the available space.
Set a readable maximum width with constraints.
Keep narrow screens fluid and test text scaling.

best_practices: Base layout decisions on available width instead of device labels or orientation alone.
Test transitions around every breakpoint in resizable windows and with larger text.
Use lazy builders for large collections and constrain content width on large screens.
anti_patterns: Do not classify layouts only as phone or tablet based on hardware type.
Do not lock orientation to hide layout defects.
Do not allow forms, text, or lists to stretch across the full large-screen width.

faq.question: When should I use LayoutBuilder?
faq.answer: Use LayoutBuilder when a widget must respond to the space allocated by its parent.

faq.question: When should I use MediaQuery.sizeOf?
faq.answer: Use MediaQuery.sizeOf when the layout decision depends on the full application window.

faq.question: Does the skill provide a universal breakpoint?
faq.answer: No. Choose breakpoints from content needs, then test nearby widths for overflow and awkward transitions.

faq.question: Can it improve large-screen lists?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends lazy responsive grids and maximum extents that adjust column counts with available width.

faq.question: Does it support foldable devices?
faq.answer: The guidance avoids orientation locks and hardware assumptions, which helps layouts respond to foldable and multi-window constraints.

faq.question: Will it run tests or validators?
faq.answer: No. It provides a validation workflow, but the user or coding agent must run project tools and inspect results.
